nodes.text: Oh, welcome, welcome. Mind the sawdust. Actually, no, don't. Sawdust on the floor means work on the bench. I'm *Tilo*. The loom, the carving bench, the worktable: all public, all yours. Sorry, I should let you speak.
What can I do for you?

choices.text: Public? Anyone can use these stations?
Your sister says you never finish anything.
You trained somewhere grand, I'd guess.

nodes.text: Anyone with the patience. That's the whole idea. A croft can't afford a loom. A *town* can afford one everybody shares. Bring hide, cloth, or timber and make what you need. Sorry, I'm talking again.

Merra told you about the chair. Of course she did. Three years, yes. Three years. But the chair is *teaching* me, you see. Every joint I cut for pay, I cut better, because the chair at home is watching. That sounded less strange in my head.

Silverfall's galleria. A clothier took me on as a boy to carry bolts up the Silver Stair. I came down before the deep trouble with one pattern-book and a needle case. Grand work up there. The useful work I learned here.
Leather, cloth, and woodcraft patterns: the whole soft-trades ladder. Priced by what they'll ask of your hands.
